blocks.text: Ladner Townhomes Under $1.2M: streets and boundaries

items.t: The search area is the strata complexes around Ladner village, in the City of Delta, under Delta Zoning Bylaw No. 7600, 2017.

blocks.text: Ladner Townhomes Under $1.2M: the housing stock

items.t: Ladner townhomes are strata homes, and services differ from houses: Delta states food scraps collection for multi-family complexes is arranged with private haulers, not the City Green Can service.
New supply comes by rezoning house lots: 715 Gilchrist Drive is proposed to Townhouse Residential 76 (RT76), for six units in two three-storey buildings.

blocks.text: Ladner Townhomes Under $1.2M: rules that affect buyers

items.t: A strata can still ban short-term rentals, though not long-term rentals. A Delta council report states rental-restriction bylaws were ended provincially, but bylaws prohibiting short-term accommodations remain permitted in all strata corporations.
The only strata age restriction now permitted is 55-and-over for seniors' housing, per the same report.

blocks.text: Ladner Townhomes Under $1.2M: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Ladner's spring clean-up slot is Tuesday, March 31, 2026, with one pick-up truck sized load per eligible household.
Extra garbage needs a sticker: two cans or bags weekly are included, and six stickers cost $7.50 at City Hall or recreation centres.
Yard trimmings drop-off is free at 4295 72 Street, Ladner.

blocks.text: Ladner Townhomes Under $1.2M: development and new projects

items.t: For the Chisholm Street Wharf construction in Ladner Village, see the ladnerforeclosuresandcourtsales note.
The 715 Gilchrist Drive rezoning was before Council on May 25, 2026, and Delta states it is consistent with the Official Community Plan.

blocks.text: Ladner Townhomes Under $1.2M: costs and taxes

items.t: Delta's 2026 flat rate utility total for a single-family home is $1,658; check which billing applies to a strata complex.
Delta property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with 5 percent penalties after July 2 and September 2, 2026.
The 601 bus runs through Ladner Exchange to Bridgeport Station via South Delta Exchange, Highway 17, Ladner Trunk Road, Highway 17A and Highway 99, per TransLink's timetable.

blocks.text: Ladner Townhomes Under $1.2M: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the complex's flood position: Delta counts 67 kilometres of dikes and seawall protecting the city.
Confirm the catchment by locator; district groupings show catchment lines run inside Ladner itself.

faq.q: Which elementary school serves a Ladner townhome address?
faq.a: It depends on the exact address; the district locator is the check. The Delta School District groups Ladner Elementary's catchment from the Hawthorne, Holly, Ladner, Port Guichon and Neilson Grove areas. Ladner Elementary is Kindergarten to Grade 7 at 5016 44 Avenue.

faq.q: Who collects garbage and food scraps at a complex?
faq.a: Garbage follows Delta's weekly system, out by 7:00 a.m. on collection day. Food scraps differ: Delta states multi-family collection is arranged with private haulers. Ask the strata who its private hauler is, what the contract costs the complex each year, and whether that cost sits inside the monthly strata fee.

faq.q: Can I run a short-term rental in a Ladner townhome?
faq.a: Check the strata bylaws first; a ban can still be valid. Delta's council report states long-term rental restrictions were ended provincially, but short-term accommodation prohibitions remain permitted in every strata corporation. A townhome that is rentable on a long-term lease may therefore still be barred from nightly or weekly rental use by its own bylaws.

faq.q: What watering rules bind the complex's lawns?
faq.a: Metro Vancouver's regional rules bind strata common property like a house lot. Stage 1 restrictions run May 1 to October 15, allow lawn watering once weekly on a designated day by address and type, and are enforced through local bylaws.

faq.q: What flood questions should I ask on a Ladner townhome?
faq.a: Whether the complex is within 30 m of a stream, slough or ditch (the Streamside Protection and Enhancement Development Permit Area), and how the strata's depreciation report and insurance treat Ladner's setting behind the City's flood-protection system — over 63 km of dikes, seawalls and foreshore protection, 31 drainage pump stations and about 538 km of drainage infrastructure.
